facts.fact: Exact nearest neighbour over high-dimensional vectors is a brute-force scan; every practical system trades recall for speed
Recall at k is the fraction of true neighbours returned; quote latency and recall together
Flat (brute force): exact, no build time, latency linear in corpus size
Flat genuinely correct below roughly 100k vectors
facts.status: unconfirmed, stated as a rule of thumb with the measured scaling

facts.fact: Flat is the baseline to measure recall against
facts.where: Reading 8 box; all recall on the page is against exact

facts.fact: HNSW is a multi-layer navigable small-world graph; search descends from a sparse top layer greedily
facts.where: Reading 9 HNSW and the animation (real algorithm on a toy)

facts.fact: HNSW is the default in pgvector, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus, Lucene, Elasticsearch
facts.where: Reading 9 correction box; system table in 14
facts.status: corrected: pgvector has no default index (you choose HNSW or IVFFlat); the others offer HNSW as their main or default graph index

facts.fact: HNSW graph lives in RAM; 1536-d float32 about 6 KB per vector; M times 8 to 12 bytes per node
facts.where: Reading 7 (6,144 and 6,152 bytes), 10 (measured bytes per vector), 14 (memory arithmetic), ANN lab calculator
facts.status: 6 KB verified and refined; 'M x 8 to 12 bytes' unconfirmed, replaced by the measured pgvector index size

facts.fact: HNSW build slow, deletes soft until rebuild
facts.status: refined: pgvector deletes are removed and the graph repaired by VACUUM (measured), REINDEX also works

facts.fact: HNSW knobs M, ef_construction, ef_search
facts.where: Reading 9 knob table; defaults 16, 64, 40; measured curves in 10 and the ANN lab

facts.fact: IVF: k-means into lists, search nprobe closest; fast build, small memory; boundary problem; drift; needs training
facts.where: Reading 9 IVF and the animation (1 and 2 probes); measured in 10
facts.status: verified (README rules lists rows/1000, probes sqrt(lists)); measured

facts.fact: IVF-PQ: subvectors replaced by codebook ids; 16x to 64x; billion vectors in RAM; lossy, rerank; classic FAISS recipe
facts.status: corrected wording: the ratio depends on the code size chosen (6,144 to 96 bytes is 64x, derived); Jegou et al. TPAMI 2011 linked; FAISS factory syntax verified

facts.fact: Scalar int8 (4x) and binary (32x) with rerank are the cheaper modern alternatives, usually first to try
facts.where: Reading 11 with measured halfvec and binary (+rerank) in pgvector; HF blog numbers

facts.fact: DiskANN (Vamana): graph on SSD, compressed vectors in RAM, about an order of magnitude less memory for a few ms; billion-scale on one node
facts.status: verified with the paper's own numbers (64 GB RAM, >5000 QPS, <3 ms, 95% 1-recall@1); 'order of magnitude' left as the paper's design, not quoted

facts.fact: DiskANN behind Azure's vector search, Milvus's disk index, pgvectorscale
facts.status: verified per vendor docs (Cosmos DB diskANN, pg_diskann GA May 2025, Milvus DISKANN, pgvectorscale StreamingDiskANN 0.9.1), plus SQL Server 2025 (preview)

facts.fact: ScaNN: anisotropic vector quantisation optimised for inner-product ranking loss
ScaNN best QPS-versus-recall on several ANN-Benchmarks tracks
facts.status: unconfirmed; dropped (ANN-Benchmarks publishes plots only); readers pointed to ANN-Benchmarks

facts.fact: ScaNN available in Postgres via pgvector's competitor extensions and in Vertex AI
facts.status: corrected: Google AlloyDB's alloydb_scann extension; Vertex AI Vector Search verified

facts.fact: Filtered search is what breaks in production; pre-filter slow when loose, post-filter empty when selective; filter during traversal or per-tenant indexes
facts.status: verified and measured (pgvector post-filter, strict and relaxed iterative scans, B-tree pre-filter at 1% and 10%)

facts.fact: Evaluate a vector store on filtered search, not unfiltered QPS
Inverted index (Lucene family): term to posting list, tf and positions for BM25 and phrase queries
Lucene segments immutable, merged in the background: LSM logic under another name
